In the Battle of the Bastards (GOT - Season 6, Episode 9), Kit Harington delivered one of the most raw, instinctive performances ever seen in television history. There’s a moment when Jon Snow gets completely buried under a pile of men  gasping, shoving, suffocating, trying to survive as chaos closes in from every side. What most people don’t know is… that fear you see on his face? It wasn’t acting. 

Kit Harington later revealed that he genuinely panicked while shooting that scene. He felt trapped, overwhelmed, and terrified and that real emotion ended up making the scene even more powerful. 

Kit said - “He is mortally afraid of crowds. It was one of the most terrifying things … 15 bearded Irishmen crushing you and when the stuntmen fell on top of him, he was actually stuck for a few moments and couldn’t move or breathe properly. He described it as one of the few times he “felt real panic on set. There’s no hero pose, no dramatic speech, no slow-motion glory. It’s just pure human desperation in the middle of a nightmare and that’s what makes this battle different. It isn’t just epic it’s primal, claustrophobic, and brutally real.

The director Miguel Sapochnik confirms that "Harington’s phobia was discussed and intentionally incorporated: “His worst fear is being buried alive … so I exploited that to its fullest  and being the amazing game-player that he is, he let me.” Which  eventually gave us pure art, and made Game of Thrones one of the most gripping and unforgettable shows ever created.
